title: The level editor's core
hints: Record a stroke's changes in a map from tile index to (first old value, latest new value) while the mouse is held; turn it into one step on release, leaving out tiles that ended where they started.
For the fill, a `std::vector<std::pair<int, int>>` used as a stack does the job: pop a tile, skip it if it is outside or not of the old kind, change it, push its four neighbours.
requirements: A stroke over many frames is one undo step, and tiles painted twice in one stroke undo to their original value.
Rectangle corners may be given in any order, and everything is clipped to the map.
Flood fill is iterative and fills only the connected region of the same kind.
Saving and loading round-trip exactly, and bad files are refused.
stretch: Add a "line" tool that paints a straight line between two tiles (Bresenham's algorithm), and a "select and move" tool that lifts a rectangle of tiles and drops it elsewhere as one undo step.
